target.name: VIHAAN KUMAR versus STATE OF HARYANA & ANR.

plain: No overruling or doubt was found in the later judgments we hold that cite this case. That is silence in what we hold, not a finding that it is good law: see the coverage block.

recent_approving.speaker: court
recent_approving.sentence: In Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana22, it was reiterated that Article 22(1) is satisfied if the accused is made aware of the arrest grounds in substance, even if not conveyed in writing.
recent_approving.next: Similarly, in Kasireddy Upender Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh23, it was observed that when arrest is made pursuant a warrant, reading out the warrant amounts to sufficient compliance.

coverage.note: Indian Kanoon's counts are typed from a screenshot of its yearly list (2026-10-05) and may include orders or duplicates; the share is a rough guide. The collection is the Supreme Court's own site to 4 May 2017 and the open Dattam Labs bucket after that, which holds only part of each year.

limits: Triage is a reading aid made by pattern rules over the sentences that name the case; it is not legal advice and not a verdict.
Only Supreme Court judgments we hold are searched; High Court treatment and judgments we lack are invisible.
Each quoted sentence was checked word for word against the judgment's text; the reading of it is a rule's, so a person must confirm.
The law reporter's case-law table (judgments of 2017 to 2023) is the reporter's annotation, not the court's words; judgments of 2024 on print no such table.
